A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TopoTune/GCCN research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, pseudocode, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v3 reports original GCCN benchmark results, architecture comparisons, performance-versus-size analyses, and training measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and reports additional GCCN evaluations in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The graph expansions, per-rank neighborhoods, GCCN update equation, and Algorithm 1 are retained. GATv2 and PNA are additional experimental choices for the existing configurable neighborhood function, without a revised GCCN procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix H.1 adds Roman Empire, Minesweeper, and Questions, substantially extending heterophilic node-classification coverage. Amazon Ratings receives absolute benchmark scores but was already evaluated in v3's Figure 10. Earlier datasets and topological domains remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a graph-only 'Best Model on TopoBench' GNN comparator. Table 8 also introduces CCNN/hypergraph comparisons for Amazon Ratings, previously shown only among GCCN configurations in Figure 10. The SCCN/CWN comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: The added evaluations use AUC-ROC for Minesweeper and Questions. Appendix H.2 tests GATv2 and PNA configurations under the stated Table 1 protocol. Existing benchmark splits, training settings, and hyperparameter search in Appendix E.3 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H.2 extends the neighborhood-function analysis by testing whether more advanced GNNs improve GCCN performance. Existing neighborhood, graph-expansion, and performance-versus-size analyses remain; the SCCN/CWN adaptation experiment is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed experiments, means with variability, and standard-deviation-based highlighting. The added tables continue these practices without introducing new uncertainty procedures or increased run counts.

E6.justification: The new GNN baseline row and Tables 8–9 substantially expand reported results; retained benchmark, model-size, and timing values are unchanged. Table 8 reports Minesweeper GCCN AUC-ROC values of 94.02±0.28 and 94.06±0.32 for cellular and simplicial domains. Table 9 adds PNA/GATv2 results, although its MUTAG best mean of 86.38 ties the retained best despite H.2 claiming outperformance.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3.4 corrects the assertion that k-GNNs match WL expressivity to matching k-WL expressivity. The principal definitions, propositions, constructions, and proofs remain. Added main-text proof summaries explain existing arguments.

C1.justification: The introduction newly presents controlled benchmarking as a distinction from prior studies using heterogeneous conditions. The central claims about systematic generalization, equivariance, expressivity, software accessibility, and parameter efficiency remain.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 now explicitly acknowledges cases where the graph GNN baseline outperforms GCCNs, qualifying their empirical advantage. Existing explanations of parameter savings, graph-expansion overhead, and lifting-related scalability limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The introduction and Section 5 replace conditional release wording and a repository pointer with code-guide/tutorial access guidance. Section 6.1 adds a specific pointer to the cited baseline tuning appendix. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for network modeling, spectral filtering, GATv2, PNA, and heterophilic benchmarks, alongside the new controlled-benchmarking contrast. The broader research positioning is retained; TopoBenchmark/TopoBench naming changes refer to the same cited work.

P1.justification: Targeted abstract/introduction edits, proof summaries, terminology corrections, acknowledgements, and appendix reorganization refine the presentation. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 8–9, expands Table 1, moves v3's appendix Table 3 into the main text as Table 2, and adjusts table headers. Figure 7's labels and references are corrected. Existing empirical plots, including Figure 10, are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added graph baseline and Appendix H evaluations broaden and better contextualize the empirical evidence. The WL correction, repaired Figure 7 references, and code guidance improve accuracy and usability. These gains outweigh limited new reporting flaws: H.2 claims MUTAG improvement despite an equal best mean, and Table 9's 'best standard GNN' NCI109 value differs from Table 1's maximum. The overall improvement is useful but incremental.
